messages:
jordan: Pushed new base image (2026.03.15) with nvidia-container-toolkit 1.11 to gpu nodepool. Seeing a subset of nodes failing containers with missing GPU libs, looks like libcuda/libnvidia-ml not mounted into the container. Affected pools: gpu-prod-usw2-a100, gpu-spot-usw2-t4. 

jordan: Example error from container start: 
```
container_linux.go:419: starting container process caused: process_linux.go:516: container init caused: rootfs_linux.go:58: mounting "/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcuda.so.1" to rootfs "/var/lib/containers/..." caused: no such file or directory
Error: could not load library "libcuda.so.1": No such file or directory
```

maya: ugh. Did the host drivers change too or just the toolkit?

jordan: Host drivers are 525.105 on most affected hosts, kernel 5.15.0-70-generic. We didn't touch drivers in this roll. The diff in the image is the toolkit package + a change to the host bind-propagation flags in the kubelet config (we tested locally).

sam: quick guess: mount propagation regression. If host mount is rprivate, containers can't see host-mounted /usr/lib/... which toolkit expects to bind. Can you `ls -l /run/nvidia/driver` on an affected node?

jordan: pasted output: 
```
root@gpu-node-12:~# ls -l /run/nvidia/driver
ls: cannot access '/run/nvidia/driver': No such file or directory
root@gpu-node-12:~# ls -l /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libnvidia-ml.so.1
-rw-r--r-- 1 root root 123456 Mar 10 12:02 /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libnvidia-ml.so.1
```

nathan: so libs exist on host but toolkit isn't binding them into container. Did the toolkit package change the expected mountpoint? Any journal logs from nvidia-container-toolkit?

jordan: grabbing journal now: 
```
Mar 15 18:02:11 gpu-node-12 nvidia-container-toolkit[1223]: nvidia-container-cli: NVML library failed to open: libnvidia-ml.so: cannot open shared object file: No such file or directory
Mar 15 18:02:11 gpu-node-12 nvidia-container-toolkit[1223]: failed to create device: no devices detected
```

maya: deploy-bot, did the rollout include kubelet config change? I remember a PR toggled hostPath mountPropagation to RPRIVATE->RSHARED.

deploy-bot: rollback triggered for node-image-rollout/gpu-nodepool-2026.03.15 by jordan at 2026-03-15T18:05:21Z :arrow_down_small: https://deploys.redwood.internal/rollouts/1234

sam: short-term workaround: cordon+drain affected nodes, reimage to previous image (2026.03.12) or add an init-script that creates symlinks inside container overlay to host libs (ugly). Longer-term we need to confirm whether the toolkit 1.11 changed the path resolution logic or our kubelet mounts got stricter.

nathan: also check containerd mount propagation in `/var/lib/kubelet/config.yaml` — if we reverted propagation accidentally for hostPaths, it will break older toolkit behavior.

jordan: rolling a canary rollback to 3 nodes now (gpu-prod-usw2-a100). Will monitor. :eyes:

maya: if rollback fixes it, let's pin toolkit to 1.10 and open an upstream issue with nvidia. If rollback doesn't fix, we need to dig into a kernel/driver mismatch.

sam: note for postmortem: include matrix of kernel version + driver + toolkit + container runtime (we saw 2 nodes with containerd 1.6.12 and the rest 1.6.13). small mismatch might be compounding.

jordan: can confirm canary rollback succeeded, containers back to normal on those 3 nodes. Rolling remainder of affected nodes now. Will follow up with logs and a short postmortem. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
